RFC 9999                       Short Notes                      June 2026


   A note is a message that one participant leaves for another without
   expecting an answer. Because no answer is expected, a sender cannot
   learn from the protocol whether a note was read, and an implementation
   that reports otherwise is reporting something it has invented rather
   than something it has observed. Senders that need an answer are
   expected to ask for one in the note itself, in whatever words their
   application uses for the purpose, and to conclude nothing from the
   silence that may follow, since a silence is not a refusal.

   Implementations are expected to keep a note until the recipient has
   asked for it or until the sender withdraws it, whichever happens
   first. A note that has been withdrawn is not an error, and a recipient
   that asks for a withdrawn note is told only that there is nothing to
   deliver, because telling it more would leak the fact that a note once
   existed. A recipient that has collected a note may ask for it again,
   and is given the same note for as long as it is kept.

RFC 9999                       Short Notes                      June 2026


   The ordering of notes between two participants is the order in which
   the sender released them, and no implementation is required to preserve
   any relationship between notes sent by different participants. Where an
   ordering is observed by a recipient, it is a property of that
   implementation and not of this protocol, and depending on it makes a
   program that works in one deployment and fails quietly in the next.
   Applications that need an ordering across participants are expected
   to carry it in the notes themselves, where every recipient can see it.

   note-message  = note-line *( note-line ) [ trailer ]
   note-line     = 1*( %x20-7E ) CRLF
   trailer       = "." CRLF
   sender-id     = ALPHA *( ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "_" )
   note-id       = 16( HEXDIG )

   The following exchange shows a note being sent and acknowledged by a
   server that has decided to keep it for the recipient to collect later.
   NOTE sender-id=alice note-id=0123456789abcdef
   200 stored, and the recipient will be told about it when next asked.
